title: Codesign of quantum error-correcting codes and modular chiplets in the presence of defects
problem: Fabrication errors in solid-state quantum devices cause significant resource overhead when scaling to fault-tolerant sizes, as traditional quantum error correction assumes perfect manufacturing. The challenge is managing defect-induced qubit quality degradation in large-scale quantum systems.
motivation: Reducing resource overhead from fabrication defects is critical for scaling quantum computers to practical fault-tolerant applications.
method: The approach codesigns quantum error-correcting codes with modular chiplet architectures, jointly optimizing the QEC procedures to account for device-specific fabrication defects. It leverages the flexibility of modular architectures to adapt QEC codes based on observed defect patterns in each chiplet, reducing the overhead required for fault tolerance.
key_novelty: Codesigning quantum error-correcting codes with modular chiplet architectures to jointly mitigate fabrication defects rather than treating them as independent concerns.
contributions: Codesign framework combining QEC code adaptation with modular chiplet architecture selection
Method for customizing quantum error correction procedures based on fabrication defect profiles
Demonstration of reduced resource overhead using modular architecture flexibility
Design methodology for fault-tolerant quantum systems resilient to manufacturing imperfections
